pr_title: [Windows] DXVA: check if HDR10 color spaces are supported by video processor
pr_body:
## Description
<!--- Provide a general summary of your change in the Pull Request title above -->
<!--- Describe your change in detail here. -->
 - In similar way that https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/23109 implements a static method to check if HDR10 color spaces are supported by video processor before initialize it. Then fallback to Pixel Shaders when DXVA not supports color conversion.
- Added support for use the two existent DXGI HDR10 color spaces with different chroma sitting: `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_YCBCR_STUDIO_G2084_LEFT_P2020` and `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_YCBCR_STUDIO_G2084_TOPLEFT_P2020`.
- When the two YCBCR HDR10 color spaces are supported is used TOPLEFT because according Microsoft documentation this is the right one for UHD Blu-Ray https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dxgicommon/ne-dxgicommon-dxgi_color_space_type#siting
- Removes the workaround for HDR10 in limited range implemented in https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/19826 because in RTX 4070 is not valid anymore (wrong black level) and even on RTX 20x, 30x is not usable now because  `CheckVideoProcessorFormatConversion` returns is not valid conversion.

## Motivation and context
Found that in NVIDIA RTX 4070 things goes wrong with HDR10 limited range.... The use of only "native" color spaces for HDR10 simplifies things and with more strictly checks and fallback to Pixel Shaders more robust and predictable behavior should result.

Closes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/23357

Also should fix other sporadic issues seen in forums as: 
https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=372606&pid=3146966#pid3146966

## How has this been tested?
Runtime tested Intel NUC8i3BEK and NVIDIA RTX 4070. 
On NUC continues working as before supporting DXVA HDR10 passthrough in full and limited range.
On RTX 4070 DXVA HDR10 works only in full range and now is used Pixel Shaders in limited range.

Note that current behavior for RTX 4070 limited range in Nexus is wrong black level and in master execution halts in:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/f84cf8bcff3c22e249d91e676c7a0229547190c1/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoRenderers/windows/RendererDXVA.cpp#L137


## What is the effect on users?
Avoids failures or wrong picture/black screen when DXVA HDR10 color conversion is not full supported and improves compatibility in some scenarios.

issue_context.title: [Windows] HDR10 passthrough using limited range is broken on NVIDIA cards in master branch
issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:

HDR10 passthrough using limited color range is broken on NVIDIA cards in master branch.

Previously was (and still) working fine with RTX 2060 on v20/Nexus



## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:

Playback fine using HDR10 passthrough with limited color range output.



## Actual Behavior
Kodi halts in `IsFormatConversionSupported`:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/d6b9189f5ca69886c4195e7695632197e27dd9f6/xbmc/cores/VideoPlayer/VideoRenderers/windows/RendererDXVA.cpp#L119

Done several extensive tests:

- This only affects NVIDIA (probably also AMD) but is working fine on Intel (NUC8i3BEK).
- In NVIDIA behavior varies depending on hardware used.
- Tested various NVIDIA drivers (535.98, 528,49, 517.48) and no differences found.

| Model        |  Driver version   | IsFormatConversionSupported | black level  |
|    :---:         |         :---:             |                   :----:                        |        :---:      |
| RTX 2060   |    535.98             |            failed                              |    correct    |
| RTX 4070   |    535.98             |            failed                              |    wrong     |

The main reason of behavior change in v21 is that color conversions are strictly validated with `IsFormatConversionSupported` also this is even more broken using newer RTX 40x because black level is wrong if bypass `IsFormatConversionSupported`

In summary: 

- In master branch is broken for all NVIDIA graphics cards.
- In Nexus seems only broken in new RTX 40x, this is probably the reason of no complaints so far.
- It seems that NVIDIA is going in the direction of not supporting HDR10 limited range output and we could say that with older RTX 20x, 30x and GTX 10x, 16x graphics, it is working fine by chance because IsFormatConversionSupported fails anyway.

## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
`IsFormatConversionSupported` seems well implemented and no issues found. Is not possible bypass / remove because in newer graphics black level obtained is wrong. Tested alternative TOPLEFT color space `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_YCBCR_STUDIO_G2084_TOPLEFT_P2020` and the result is the same.

I have some idea that I have tried and it works but I need to think about how to implement it correctly since it could cause other side effects, basically is always use full range in the video driver and move range conversion to swap chain. This is move this functionality  from video driver to Win32 API then it is very unlikely that there will be behavior variations due different hardware.



### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
1. Configure limited color range in settings 
2. Play HDR10 video in a setup that supports HDR passthrough



### Debuglog
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
<!--- A debuglog is always mandatory when creating an issue. Provide one! -->
The debuglog can be found here:

https://paste.kodi.tv/edawolasid.kodi

### Screenshots 
Here are some links or screenshots to help explain the problem:
<!--- Put your text below this line -->



## Additional context or screenshots (if appropriate)
Here is some additional context or explanation that might help:
<!--- How has this bug affected you? What were you trying to accomplish? -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->



### Your Environment
Used Operating system:

 - [ ] Android
 - [ ] iOS
 - [ ] tvOS
 - [ ] Linux
 - [ ] macOS
 - [X] Windows
 - [ ] Windows UWP

 - Operating system version/name:  Windows 11 22H2
 - Kodi version: v21

comments:
The description doesn't say, but this is a dxva-only problem, correct? Pixel shaders are fine?
Strange result with RTX 2060.

I think there are 2 separate points.

1/ what to do with the return value of IsFormatConversionSupported 
2/ what to do about limited range and dxva processor lacking support

For 1/ I think we're in agreement that in preparation for release, an unsupported conversion should not fail Configure() but only log a warning for an unsupported conversion and possible fallback to an imperfect conversion.

For 2/
The API for the swap chain color space is Windows 10+ only. Windows 8.1 is still supported in v21, so the solution doesn't seem practical.

For my AMD, the rendering falls back to Pixel Shaders in your scenario. IsBT2020Supported() called by GetWeight() returns false.
IsBT2020Supported() makes the assumption that a processor support for RGB Studio SDR output is always the same as support for RGB Studio HDR output. For my AMD it's true.
The assumption is broken with the RTX 4070. It supports full and studio in SDR, but only full in HDR (see your log output of CProcessorHD::ListSupportedConversions)
IsBT2020Supported was originally meant to check HDR to SDR options, not HDR to HDR.

Another strange thing in your log:
> DXVA::CProcessorHD::IsFormatConversionSupported: conversion from P010 / YCBCR_STUDIO_G22_LEFT_P2020 to R10G10B10A2_UNORM / RGB_STUDIO_G22_NONE_P2020 is NOT supported

For passthrough of HDR, G22 transfer is unexpected, instead of G2084. There is no need to avoid tone-mapping by dxva in a passthrough situation. The G22 transfer test happens because of InitProcessor setting m_bSupportHDR10Limited to false. Same thing happens on my AMD if I bypass the GetWeight() check.

Even if that changed, the RTX4070 would still answer false to IsFormatConversionSupported(), but maybe the processor would fallback on full range and give a picture.

So for solutions, I'd say, either:
a/ fix GetWeight/IsBT2020Supported to return false and fallback to pixel shaders
or
b/ make dvxa processor output full range and have the output shader convert the range.

drawback of a/: can't use the fancy dxva scalers with limited output since they are coupled with dxva color conversion in dxva render method.
however a/ is less intrusive.

possible solution / workaround c/ Set Kodi in full range and rely on the GPU driver's output format for the conversion (select RGB full or limited in driver's control panel).
Might be problematic for legacy drivers and drivers provided by Microsoft / Windows Update without the vendor control panel, as I don't remember a range selection in Windows' standard control panel.

> Another strange thing in your log:
> 
> DXVA::CProcessorHD::IsFormatConversionSupported: conversion from P010 / YCBCR_STUDIO_G22_LEFT_P2020 to R10G10B10A2_UNORM / RGB_STUDIO_G22_NONE_P2020 is NOT supported

This is because previously is checked support of `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_STUDIO_G2084_NONE_P2020` and if not supported is used `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_STUDIO_G22_NONE_P2020` as fallback. Two bad things here: is a assumed `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_STUDIO_G22_NONE_P2020` always is supported and is assumed correct picture. This as worked for a while witch GTX 10x, RTX 20 but not in RTX 4070.

I'm preparing a PR that eliminates this workaround (as is not valid anymore) and fallback to Pixel Shaders in GetWeight. 

I have discarded the initial idea I had (conversion in swap chain) for various reasons:

- Too complicated.
- It's another workaround.
- Double video range conversion: limited to full (in driver) and full to limited in swap chain.

Is supposed that main reason of use limited range is avoid unnecessary video conversions and improve precision (avoid errors due scale change and quantization).

Then for HDR10 in DXVA only "nominal" color spaces will be used `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_STUDIO_G2084_NONE_P2020` and `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_FULL_G2084_NONE_P2020` depending on output range and if these are not supported will be fallback to Pixel Sahders. 

This will simplify things and avoid "unexpected" results.

Yes might as well not put too much effort in it - not sure how many people use the limited mode, probably only "bit perfect" purists.
Agreed that it looks like manufacturers are gradually removing support for limited RGB.

@wojtekLs I would guess because it's not a common use case. Computer screens are full range.

For bit perfect, it looks like these days you can stay in NV12 or P010 without back and forth conversions from decode up to the display. Then the display internally convert the YCbCr to RGB to drive the screen, same way it does for a bluray source. Kodi doesn't support that mode and it feels like a significant change.

review_comments: Same question about using picture.chroma_sitting or not.

This function is called after switching screen SDR to HDR so assuming output format = back buffer = rgb10 works but doesn't feel very strong.
The log looks odd in SDR for AMD and 8 bit backbuffer ("Use 10 bit for SDR" Auto or off value) because the processor has no support for PQ in B8G8R8A8_UNORM. Odd but not blocking.
Same note as IsHDR10PassthroughSupported(), assuming the input format is always P010.
This code is only to determine use Left or TopLeft and if `dxgi_format` is not supported is detected early in `IsHDR10PassthroughSupported()` and this code is not reached anyway.

AMD supports both variants,

H264/265 have a chroma sitting attribute, accessible as picture.chroma_location, see enum AVChromaLocation, AVCHROMA_LOC_TOPLEFT = 3.
AV1 has chroma_sample_position / CSP_COLOCATED, don't have samples to check if available the same way through ffmpeg.
Shouldn't that be used to find the preferred color space? Maybe some files are badly flagged though.

If the processor doesn't support the preferred, then the other one is an acceptable fallback I suppose and doesn't warrant using Pixel Shaders instead, which don't take chroma sitting into account anyway.
This is matter for another PR. I take a look another time.
nevermind I'm OK with topleft for everything. We'll see later if it's a problem.
Please also log which one is chosen in m_HDR10Left (in case both are supported)
